- All flagged findings are resolved or documented with an accepted justification.
- The scan results are consistent with the legal clearance conditions; any contradiction is escalated back to the legal decision record before productization proceeds.
- Clearance evidence is stored where the release/process gates can reference it.

## Description

This epic onboards the fallback object store's midstream repository to Konflux so the bundled store's image is built through the standard product build pipeline. It executes only if the legal review selects the Apache-2.0 fallback candidate, and runs in parallel with the image productization work — the build pipeline is available when the productized image is ready to publish.

- Onboard the fallback store's midstream repository to Konflux using the known onboarding recipe: application and component definitions, build pipeline configuration, and integration configuration.
- Configure the container image build for the store from the midstream source.
- Wire the standard checks applicable to an image build (as per the Konflux onboarding recipe) and verify the pipeline builds the image end to end.
- Do not gate the productization code work on this onboarding — the two proceed in parallel and are coupled only through the build pipeline's green state when the image publishes.

- The Konflux build pipeline builds the fallback store's container image from the midstream source end to end.

- The pipeline can produce a pinned digest for the built image so the operator configuration can reference it.

# Legal review: redistribution posture for bundling the AGPL-3.0 candidate object store

## Description

This epic resolves the licensing question that blocks all shipping work for the bundled S3-compatible object store. The leading candidate, MinIO, is AGPL-3.0 licensed; redistribution terms must be cleared for the product's distribution model before any productization work can ship, and the outcome may force a different upstream. This investigation produces the documented legal decision that selects which store the platform bundles.

## Scope

- Complete legal review of redistributing the candidate object store (MinIO, AGPL-3.0) within the product's distribution model for disconnected installs.
- Determine and document the derivative-work posture for operator integration — specifically whether bundling, enabling, and managing the store through the Platform Operator, and any operator code that integrates with it, creates derivative-work obligations under AGPL-3.0.
- Evaluate distribution scenarios relevant to disconnected installs: shipping the container image in the product payload, mirrored registries, and customer air-gapped re-distribution.
- Produce a documented, reviewable decision (with legal sign-off) covering: whether AGPL-3.0 redistribution is acceptable; under what conditions; and if not, the recommendation to adopt the Apache-2.0 fallback candidate (e.g. SeaweedFS), which restarts image productization on the new upstream.
- If the fallback is selected, confirm the fallback candidate's license (and licensing of its transitive dependencies at a coarse level) supports redistribution before handing off to the productization work.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The legal review is completed and documented, covering redistribution of the AGPL-3.0 candidate and the derivative-work posture for operator integration (HLR-1).
- The decision explicitly names one of exactly two outcomes: (a) AGPL-3.0 redistribution cleared under stated conditions, or (b) AGPL terms cannot be satisfied and the Apache-2.0 fallback candidate is selected.
- The decision record identifies which downstream work changes under the selected outcome — the store's midstream onboarding, productized image, and the operator/consumer integration specifics — so implementation teams know which upstream to target.
- Legal sign-off is recorded on the decision.
- If outcome (b): the fallback candidate is named and its license compatibility for redistribution is confirmed in the decision record.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): Legal review of redistributing the candidate object store (MinIO, AGPL-3.0) is completed and documented, including the derivative-work posture for operator integration. This clearance blocks all shipping work.

# Platform Operator enablement of the bundled S3-compatible object store

## Description

This epic makes the bundled S3-compatible object store a supported, administrator-enabled capability of the platform. Administrators of disconnected and PoC clusters can enable the store through the Platform Operator, backed by a productized image and a managed upgrade lifecycle — replacing today's unsupported, ad hoc upstream installs.

## Scope

- Design and implement the Platform Operator enablement path for the bundled S3-compatible object store: the administrator-facing opt-in that deploys and manages the store on clusters where no customer-provided S3-compatible storage exists.
- Consume the productized store image for the upstream selected by the completed legal review (the AGPL-3.0 candidate if cleared, otherwise the Apache-2.0 fallback), pinned by image digest.
- Implement the upgrade lifecycle for the bundled store: version progression of the store and its configuration across platform releases, including upgrades of disconnected installs.
- Define the operator's management surface for the store: deployment, configuration, health/status reporting, and teardown/disable.
- Keep the store optional and administrator-controlled: enabling it must not affect clusters that use customer-provided storage, and disabling it must be a supported operation (with clear behavior for existing data, documented per the documentation work).
- Sizing and resource guidance for the store is consumed (and surfaced to administrators where applicable) consistent with the sizing guidance produced for documentation.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a disconnected or PoC cluster with no S3-compatible storage, when an administrator enables the bundled store through the Platform Operator, then a supported S3-compatible object store is deployed and reported healthy, measured by a successful operator-driven deployment without manual manifest application.
- Given the bundled store is enabled, when the platform is upgraded, then the bundled store is upgraded through the operator lifecycle without requiring reinstall, measured by an upgrade test on a disconnected cluster.
- Given a cluster using customer-provided storage, when the bundled store capability is not enabled, then the cluster's storage configuration is unchanged (no store resources deployed, no interference with existing storage), measured by a not-enabled installation check.
- A pinned image digest for the productized store image of the selected upstream is available and referenced by the operator configuration.
- The bundled store's endpoint, as exposed by the operator, is usable by platform components as a connection target (validated by the consumer components' connection-default work measured against this endpoint).
- Workloads that depend on S3-compatible storage continue functioning when connections target the bundled store, including the surfaces where those workloads appear (pipeline runs and model serving status views), measured by an end-to-end check on a cluster using the bundled store.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P0): Administrators can enable a supported, bundled S3-compatible object store through the Platform Operator, with productized images and upgrade lifecycle.
- Passive validation (Dashboard, listed in the strategy's Affected Components): pipeline and model serving views continue functioning when connections target the bundled store.
